examples.en: You must slow down in a school zone.
The driver slowed down before the curve.
When it rains, cars pass slowly.
The train began to slow down as it neared the station.
It's dangerous to run without slowing down.
The bicycle is slowing down before the downhill road.

explain: 주로 차나 기차의 속도를 줄일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 도로 표지판에는 '감속'이라고만 써 있고, 일상에서는 '속도를 줄이다'가 더 흔해요. 반대말은 '가속하다'예요.

phrases.en: When it rains, you have to slow down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감속하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상에서 훨씬 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 감속하다, but much more common in daily life.

phrases.en: I lower my speed on curves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차의 속도를 일부러 낮출 때 써요. '속도를 줄이다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you deliberately lower a vehicle's speed. Similar to 속도를 줄이다.

phrases.en: There's construction ahead, so please slow down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송이나 표지판처럼 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request, like in announcements or signs.

explain_en: 감속하다 is mainly for cars and trains reducing speed. Road signs just say 감속, while in daily talk 속도를 줄이다 is more common. The opposite is 가속하다.

examples.ko: 사고가 나서 경찰이 교통정리를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: There was an accident, so the police are directing traffic.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 차가 많아서 교통정리가 필요해요.
examples.en: During rush hour there are many cars, so traffic control is needed.
A man helped direct traffic in front of the construction site.

examples.ko: 이 사거리는 교통정리가 잘 안 돼서 늘 복잡해요.
examples.en: Traffic isn't managed well at this intersection, so it's always chaotic.
On festival days, volunteers take charge of directing traffic.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오는 날에는 교통정리 인원이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: On days with heavy rain, more people are needed to direct traffic.

explain: 길에서 차와 사람이 잘 다니도록 신호를 보내 주는 일을 말해요. 경찰이나 도우미가 손짓으로 하는 모습이 먼저 떠올라요. 복잡한 일이나 의견을 정리할 때도 비유로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 의견이 너무 많아서 팀장님이 교통정리를 했어요.
phrases.en: There were too many opinions, so the team leader sorted things out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡하게 얽힌 의견이나 일을 한 번에 정리해 주는 것을 말해요. 회사나 모임에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means sorting out tangled opinions or tasks in one go. You often hear it at work or in meetings.
phrases.en_equiv: sort things out; untangle the mess

explain_en: It refers to guiding cars and people with signals so they can move smoothly, like a police officer waving traffic through. People also use it figuratively for sorting out a messy situation or many opinions.

examples.en: Turn on your turn signal before changing lanes.
I was startled because the car ahead didn't even use its signal.
The turn signal broke, so I went to the repair shop.
The right turn signal stays on.
When driving I hear the clicking of the turn signal.
I keep forgetting to turn on the turn signal.

explain: 운전할 때 방향을 알리는 등을 말하는 구어체예요. 공식 이름은 '방향지시등'이지만 일상에서는 거의 '깜빡이'라고 해요. '켜다'와 같이 써서 '깜빡이를 켜다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I turned on the turn signal before turning left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깜빡이와 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase with 깜빡이.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn on the turn signal

phrases.en: After changing lanes, you turn off the turn signal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 켠 깜빡이를 끌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when turning the signal off.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn off the turn signal

phrases.en: On the test, you have to write 'directional signal'.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜빡이'의 공식 이름으로, 시험이나 설명서에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name for 깜빡이, used in tests and manuals.

explain_en: It is the casual word for the light that signals your direction when driving. The formal term is 방향지시등, but in daily life nearly everyone says 깜빡이. The usual phrase is 깜빡이를 켜다.

examples.en: Turn right at that intersection.
A new coffee shop opened at the intersection.
The meeting spot is the intersection in front of City Hall.
The bank is right after you pass the intersection.
The intersection gets very congested at rush hour.

examples.ko: 네거리 신호등이 고장 나서 경찰이 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The traffic light at the intersection broke, so a police officer stood there.

explain: 네거리는 길이 네 방향으로 만나는 곳이고, 세 방향이면 '삼거리'라고 해요. 길을 알려 줄 때는 '사거리'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Turn left at the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고, 말할 때는 '사거리'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but '사거리' is more common in speech.

phrases.en: I wait for the light at the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '에서' to show the place where something happens.

phrases.en: The traffic light at the intersection is broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 장소에 있는 것을 말할 때 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it in front to name something located at that spot.

explain_en: 네거리 is where roads meet in four directions; with three it is '삼거리'. When giving directions people say '사거리' more often.

examples.ko: 차가 비탈길을 다 내려와 다시 오르막길을 오르기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The car came all the way down the slope and started climbing an uphill road again.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 비탈길은 미끄러우니 조심하세요.
examples.en: Sloped roads are slippery on rainy days, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 비탈길이 너무 가팔라서 자전거는 끌고 가야 해요.
examples.en: This slope is so steep that you have to walk your bike.
The bus slowly goes up the narrow sloped road.

examples.ko: 짐을 들고 비탈길 끝까지 올라가니 숨이 찼어요.
examples.en: Carrying my luggage all the way up the slope, I was out of breath.
There are steps on every sloped road in the neighborhood.

explain: '오르막길'과 '내리막길'은 방향을 말하지만, '비탈길'은 올라가든 내려가든 경사진 길 전체를 가리켜요. 눈이나 비 오는 날 미끄럽다는 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Climbing the slope left me out of breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기울어진 길을 올라가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going up a sloped road.

phrases.example: 자전거로 비탈길을 내려갈 때는 속도를 줄이세요.
phrases.en: Slow down when going down a slope on a bike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내려갈 때도 같은 '비탈길'을 써서 방향과 상관없이 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word works going down, so it fits either direction.

phrases.example: 집 앞이 가파른 비탈길이라 겨울에는 위험해요.
phrases.en: The road in front of my house is a steep slope, so it's dangerous in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가파른'을 붙이면 경사가 심하다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '가파른' makes it clear the slope is steep.

explain_en: '오르막길' (uphill) and '내리막길' (downhill) show direction, but '비탈길' refers to the whole sloped road whether you go up or down. It often comes up when talking about slippery roads in rain or snow.

examples.en: I sat by the pond and watched the fish.
The children play catching frogs at the edge of the pond.
In the evening I walked slowly along the pond.
We ate our lunch under the willow tree by the pond.
It rained, so the area around the pond is muddy.

examples.ko: 연못가 벤치는 우리가 자주 만나는 곳이에요.
examples.en: The bench by the pond is where we often meet.

explain: '강가', '바닷가', '길가'처럼 '-가'가 붙어 물 둘레의 가장자리를 말해요. '연못가에서', '연못가를 따라'처럼 장소를 나타내는 조사와 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I took pictures at the edge of the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 한 일을 말할 때 조사 '에서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 에서 to say what you did there.
phrases.en_equiv: at the edge of the pond

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the edge of the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장자리를 따라 이동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving along the edge.

phrases.en: There is a bench next to the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연못가'보다 위치를 간단하게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way of giving a location than 연못가.

explain_en: Like '강가', '바닷가' and '길가', the '-가' ending means the edge or surroundings of the water. It often appears with place particles, as in '연못가에서' and '연못가를 따라'.

examples.en: Please make a U-turn at the next intersection.
I took a wrong road, so I made a hurried U-turn.
You can't make a U-turn here.
The taxi suddenly made a U-turn and I was startled.
I tried to make a U-turn, but there were too many cars.
Don't make a U-turn, go straight a bit more.

explain: 택시를 탔을 때 '여기서 유턴해 주세요'라고 자주 말해요. '유턴을 하다'로 나눠 써도 같아요. 길에서 반대 방향으로 돌 때만 쓰고, 마음이 바뀌어서 돌아가는 일에는 보통 '돌아가다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Driver, please make a U-turn up ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택시나 차에서 부탁할 때 쓰는 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request used in a taxi or car.

phrases.en: If you make a U-turn there, my house is right there.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유턴하다'를 둘로 나눈 말로 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The split form of '유턴하다' with the same meaning.

phrases.en: You can make a U-turn on this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유턴이 가능한 곳인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a U-turn is allowed or possible.

explain_en: When riding a taxi you often say '여기서 유턴해 주세요'. Splitting it as '유턴을 하다' means the same. It is for turning the car around on the road; for changing your mind and going back, people usually say '돌아가다'.

examples.en: I needed nails, so I went to the hardware store.
The hardware store owner showed me how to use it.
I had a key copied at the neighborhood hardware store.
The hardware store closes at seven.
I'm looking for a hardware store to buy a light bulb.
Where is the nearest hardware store?

explain: 집을 고칠 때 쓰는 못, 망치, 전구 같은 작은 도구를 사거나 열쇠를 복사하러 가는 동네 가게예요. 큰 마트에서도 팔지만 필요한 걸 말하면 사장님이 골라 주는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: I bought a light bulb at the neighborhood hardware store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 작은 가게라는 느낌을 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of a small nearby shop.

phrases.en: I'll stop by the hardware store on my way home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 가게에 들러서 필요한 것을 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a quick stop to buy something needed.
phrases.en_equiv: to stop by the hardware store

phrases.en: The hardware store owner copied my key.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 주인을 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to refer to the shop owner.

explain_en: This is a neighborhood shop where you buy small tools like nails, hammers and bulbs, or get a key copied. Big supermarkets sell some of these too, but here the owner picks the right item when you describe what you need.

en: steering wheel; handlebars (not a door handle)

examples.ko: 운전할 때는 핸들을 두 손으로 잡으세요.
examples.en: When driving, hold the steering wheel with both hands.
The steering wheel on this car is too heavy.
I swerved suddenly and avoided an accident.
I hung my bag on the bicycle handlebars.

examples.ko: 핸들 위치를 내 키에 맞게 조절했어요.
examples.en: I adjusted the steering wheel position to my height.
The steering wheel is made of leather, so it is not slippery.

explain: 한국어 '핸들'은 자동차 운전대와 자전거·오토바이의 손잡이 막대를 말해요. 영어 handle처럼 문이나 가방의 손잡이를 '핸들'이라고 하면 어색하고, 그때는 '손잡이'라고 해요. '핸들을 잡다', '핸들을 꺾다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 앞에 장애물이 있어서 핸들을 급하게 꺾었어요.
phrases.en: There was an obstacle ahead, so I turned the steering wheel sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전 중 방향을 갑자기 크게 바꿀 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you suddenly change direction while driving.

phrases.en: To go right, turn the steering wheel slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꺾다'보다 부드럽게 방향을 바꾸는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels gentler than 꺾다; a normal turn of the wheel.

phrases.en: The bicycle handlebars were wobbly, so I fixed them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차뿐 아니라 자전거의 손잡이 막대도 '핸들'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides cars, the handlebars of a bicycle are also called 핸들.

explain_en: Korean '핸들' means a car's steering wheel or the handlebars of a bicycle or motorbike. Calling a door or bag handle a '핸들' is wrong; that is '손잡이'. Use it as '핸들을 잡다' or '핸들을 꺾다'.
